# `@jterrazz/test` — rule reference

> Generated from `src/lint/manifest.ts` by `npm run docs` — every mechanized convention across the four enforcement channels (statique · checker · runtime · process). Rule ids are stable: cite them in suppressions and reviews. Narrative lives in `docs/12-conventions.md` (the constitution) and `docs/13-linting.md` (the static plugin + checker).

## A — Creating runners

| Code | Implementation                 | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Fix                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | ------------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A1   | `a1-specification-file`        | statique | A runner is created only in a `*.specification.ts(x)` file under `specs/`: calling `specification.*` anywhere else is an error. The `.tsx` spelling is the same file with a `wrap` written in JSX. A `component`-role file is out of reach: a rendered unit starts nothing.                                                             | Move the call into `specs/<facet>/<facet>.specification.ts` and export the handle from there.                         |
| A2   | `a2-known-constructors`        | statique | Six constructors and only six: `specification.api()`, `specification.jobs()`, `specification.cli(bin)`, `specification.integration()`, `specification.website()`, `specification.mobile()`. Any other member (`.app`, `.http`, `.stack`…) is an error. A rendered component starts nothing: it is a chain, not a member of this record. | Name one of the six, or reach for the `component` chain — a seventh subject is a decision before it is a constructor. |
| A3   | `a3-no-destructure-alias`      | statique | The return is destructured under the constructor's canonical name, unaliased (`{ api, cleanup, docker }`); renaming (`{ api: myApi }`) is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                     | Drop the alias and keep the canonical name.                                                                           |
| A4   | `a4-cleanup-afterall`          | statique | The specification file passes `cleanup` to `afterAll`; a `cleanup` destructured but never handed over is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Add `afterAll(cleanup)` at the end of the specification file.                                                         |
| A9   | `a9w-redundant-root`           | statique | A `root` pointing at the directory the automatic walk would have found is redundant → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Drop the option: the walk finds the nearest `package.json` by itself.                                                 |
| A7   | `a7-database-property`         | checker  | With ≥ 2 databases, `database:` is required on every `.seed()`/`.table()`; with exactly one it is forbidden — checked by crossing the `services:` record with the calls in the tests.                                                                                                                                                   | State `database:` everywhere or nowhere, whichever the record calls for.                                              |
| A7   | `a7-database-runtime`          | runtime  | The framework throws at run time if `database:` is absent with ≥ 2 databases, or present with exactly one (it doubles the checker channel).                                                                                                                                                                                             | State `database:` everywhere or nowhere, whichever the record calls for.                                              |
| A8   | `a8-services-type-the-factory` | type     | The `services` record types the factory argument: `server: (services) => …` sees exactly the keys the record declares.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Declare the service in the record, or read the key that is there.                                                     |
| A11  | `a11-server-xor-url`           | type     | `server` and `url` are mutually exclusive on `specification.website()` — the pair is inexpressible, not runtime-checked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                | State `server` for a site this run starts, `url` for one already running.                                             |

## B — Spec chains

| Code | Implementation              | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Fix                                                                                                                |
| ---- | --------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| B2   | `b2-known-fixture-marker`   | statique | An unknown `$…` marker in a literal passed to `.fixture()` is an error (`$FIXTURES` is the only one).                                                                                                                                                                                  | Write `$FIXTURES/<name>` for the shared pool, or a path relative to the spec for local ground.                     |
| B4   | `b4-given-then`             | statique | Every test carries `// Given -` then `// Then -` (both, in that order); a Given declared after a Then is an error. A `test.each` table is judged ONCE, on the table, not once per row. A `<case>.spec.yaml` document has no comments: its narration is its `description:`.             | Write the two markers, in order, as sentences about the subject — not about the code (chapter 12 § The narration). |
| B6   | `b6w-redundant-env-url`     | statique | `.env({ <SERVICE>_URL: ….connectionString })` repeats the framework's own injection → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                         | Drop the line: the record key already injects `<KEY>_URL` into the child process.                                  |
| B8   | `b8-kebab-trigger`          | statique | `.trigger(name)` takes a stable kebab-case identifier; a non-kebab-case `name` is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                            | Write the job name in kebab-case, the same spelling the application registers it under.                            |
| B9   | `b9w-product-command`       | statique | A `specification.cli(bin)` whose binary resolves inside a dependency's `node_modules/.bin` tests the third-party tool, not the product command → warning (a suppression with a reason is accepted).                                                                                    | Point the runner at the product's own binary; assert on a tool's output through `result.grep`.                     |
| B10  | `b10-when-between-markers`  | statique | A `// When -` marker is optional; written, it sits after `// Given -` and before `// Then -`.                                                                                                                                                                                          | Move it to the action it narrates, or drop it when the chain is the action.                                        |
| B11  | `b11-marker-one-line`       | statique | A marker is exactly one line: a `//` comment directly under one, at the same indentation, is a wrapped marker and an error. A tool’s directive is not a sentence — a linter’s `-disable`/`-enable`, a formatter’s `-ignore`, a `@ts-` pragma and a coverage line stand where they are. | Fold the continuation into the sentence, or separate it with a blank line.                                         |
| B5   | `b5-await-using-inference`  | checker  | B5's one channel: docker-aware runners are inferred from the `docker:` option of the imported specification file, and every `.exec()` result bound without `await using` is reported.                                                                                                  | Bind the result with `await using`, so the containers the run spawned are disposed with the scope.                 |
| B2   | `b2-unknown-marker-runtime` | runtime  | The framework refuses at run time an unknown `$…` marker, or a `$FIXTURES` with no ancestor `specs` directory (with a guiding message).                                                                                                                                                | Write `$FIXTURES/<name>`, from a spec that sits under a `specs/` tree.                                             |
| B6   | `b6-url-injection`          | runtime  | In `cli` mode with `services`, the framework injects `<KEY>_URL` (camel-aware CONSTANT_CASE) plus the unambiguous aliases `DATABASE_URL`/`REDIS_URL`; `.env()` overrides (`null` unsets).                                                                                              | Read the variable the record key injects; state `.env()` only to override or unset it.                             |
| B7   | `b7-sequence-by-seed`       | runtime  | A sequence is expressed by SEEDING the state the second run would have found: every chain starts on databases the framework has reset.                                                                                                                                                 | Seed the state the earlier step would have left, and open one chain per action.                                    |
| B1   | `b1-one-terminal-action`    | type     | Exactly ONE terminal action closes a chain: what it answers is a result, and a result carries no verbs to continue with.                                                                                                                                                               | Open a second chain for a second action.                                                                           |
| B3   | `b3-no-label-on-a-chain`    | type     | A chain carries no label: the test name is the sentence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Name the test; the chain states what it does, not what it is called.                                               |

## C — Files & folders

| Code | Implementation                 | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---- | ------------------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1   | `c1-domain-structure`          | statique | A specs tree DECLARES its shape through the `depth` option: `facet-domain` (the default — a test at facet/domain depth, a `*.specification.ts` at the facet root), `facet` (a test at the facet root OR one domain folder down, never deeper), `mirror` (a test at any depth ≥ 1, named after its directory), `off`. In every mode, `off` included: a directory with a leading underscore is GROUND, never a domain — no spec lives inside one. One exception, and only one: ground may be CODE, and a `<module>.test.ts` sitting BESIDE the `<module>.ts` it tests is legal there (that is I2). A test with no neighbouring module, or a `*.specification.ts`, is still a violation. A `.test.tsx` is out of reach: a rendered unit is specified beside its component, never in a facet/domain tree — I2 holds its neighbourhood. | Move the file to the depth the tree declares, or declare the depth the tree actually has.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| C2   | `c2-http-only-requests`        | statique | `_requests/` holds `.http` files only; any other extension is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Write the request as a complete `.http` document, or move the file to `_fixtures/`.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| C4   | `c4-contract-shape`            | statique | Under `specs/**/contracts/`: the ROOT carries only `*.contracts.ts` facades (a default export built by `defineContracts(...)` or a composition re-export; named exports are scenarios) and the provider folders `http` \| `openai` \| `anthropic`. A unit contract is `<provider>/<kebab-name>.ts` with an `export default defineContract(...)` (or a factory returning one), and its `request` builder must name the provider of its own folder. A provider folder is flat and holds only `*.ts` and `*.response.json`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Move the file to the half it belongs to: a facade at the root, a unit under its provider.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| C6   | `c6-tomatch-extension`         | statique | `toMatch`'s argument carries its extension (`'help.txt'`, `'<case>.aria.yaml'` for a tree golden), except for a directory snapshot; a file subject with no extension is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Write the fixture's full name, extension included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| C7   | `c7-seeds-sql-only`            | statique | `_seeds/` holds `*.sql` files only; any other file is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Write the seed as SQL, or move the file to `_fixtures/` as the material it is.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| C8   | `c8-referenced-fixture-exists` | statique | A literal passed to `.request`/`.seed`/`.fixture`/`toMatch` must exist on disk under its conventional root; a missing path is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Create the file, or fix the name — the message prints the path it looked for.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| C10  | `c10-contracts-boundary`       | statique | Outside `specs/**/contracts/`, an import resolving into a provider folder (`contracts/{http,openai,anthropic}/…`) is an error: a test imports only the `*.contracts.ts` facades.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Add a named scenario export to the facade and import that instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| C11  | `c11-contract-data-pairing`    | statique | Inside a provider folder, every `*.response.json` and every `*.request.ts` has a `<stem>.ts` sibling — the stem is the name up to the FIRST dot (`events.fr.response.json` → `events.ts`). Orphan data is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Write the contract that serves the payload, or delete the payload.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| C13  | `c13-underscored-ground`       | statique | Under `specs/`, a spec's ground carries a leading underscore: `_fixtures/`, `_expected/`, `_requests/`, `_seeds/`. | C8   | `c8-spec-registered-name`      | checker  | A document's bare `env:` words and `serve:` names are keys of the `env`/`serve` objects of a `specification.cli(…)` in the nearest directory carrying `*.specification.ts` files (literals read statically; ignored otherwise).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Register the name in the specification, or fix the spelling.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| C9   | `c9-dead-fixtures`             | checker  | No dead fixtures: every file under `_seeds/`/`_requests/`/`_fixtures/` and every top-level entry of `_expected/` must be referenced; a feature directory with no test file and no `*.spec.yaml` is an orphan (a warning when the argument is not a literal). A `<case>.spec.yaml` references the fixtures its `fixture:` entries name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Reference it from the spec it stands under, or delete it.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| C12  | `c12-spec-file-name`           | checker  | The suffix says the kind, and the tree agrees with it. A `.spec.ts` — the ASSEMBLED product — lives under `specs/<facet>/`; anywhere else is an error. A `.test.ts` — the UNIT — lives beside its module; under a facet folder (`api`, `cli`, `integration`, `jobs`, `mobile`, `website`) it is an error, fixable by `--fix` (a `git mv`). A `.test.ts` that reaches no runner is C18’s, whose fix is the opposite move, and the mover leaves it alone. A first level that is NOT a facet is a repository suite: it covers a tree, keeps `.test.ts`, and C1’s declared depth is what judges it. A document is named `<case>.spec.yaml`: `<case>` in kebab-case, without the words `test`/`spec`/`cli` the suffix already carries, and never the bare name of its directory.                                                        | Move the `.spec.ts` under `specs/<facet>/` (or rename it `.test.ts` beside its module); rename the facet `.test.ts` to `.spec.ts` — `jterrazz-test-check <root> --fix` does it with `git mv`, and names every include glob of the member that still says `.test.ts`. |
| C14  | `c14-pool-fixture-shared`      | checker  | A pool fixture is SHARED, or it is local: a directory of `<specs>/_fixtures/` referenced (`$FIXTURES/<name>`) from a single spec directory — two documents of one leaf count as one — must live beside that leaf, at `<leaf>/_fixtures/<name>/`, referenced by the relative form. Zero references is the dead-fixture error (C9). Fixed by `--fix`: the directory is moved and the literals rewritten.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Run `jterrazz-test-check <root> --fix`; it moves the directory and rewrites what named it.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| C15  | `c15-local-fixture-reach`      | checker  | A local fixture is read only from its own directory: a `fixture:`/`.fixture()` path containing `..`, or whose target leaves the `_fixtures/` of the spec naming it, is an error — ground shared by several leaves goes in the `$FIXTURES` pool.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Copy it under this leaf's own `_fixtures/`, or promote it to the pool.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| C16  | `c16-document-outside-ground`  | checker  | A `<case>.spec.yaml` is a SPEC, not ground: a document under `_expected/`, `_requests/`, `_seeds/` or `_fixtures/` is an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Move the document beside the test that runs it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

| C21  | `c21w-ground-owned-by-one`     | checker  | Ground in a leaf holding ≥ 2 node tests (`.test.ts`, `.spec.ts`) that a single one of them reads is a warning. ## D — Assertions

| Code | Implementation                       | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Fix                                                                                                                                     |
| ---- | ------------------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D2   | `d2-await-io-matcher`                | statique | An IO matcher (`toMatchRows`/`toBeEmpty`/`toBeRunning`) must be awaited or returned; otherwise the assertion never runs → error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Put `await` in front of the `expect(...)`.                                                                                              |
| D2   | `d2w-await-sync-matcher`             | statique | `await` on an always-synchronous matcher (`toBe`/`toEqual`/`toContain`/`toHaveLength`) is redundant → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Drop the `await`.                                                                                                                       |
| D6   | `d6w-transform-token-equivalent`     | statique | A `transform` that only rewrites into equivalents of the standard tokens duplicates the grammar → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Delete the transform and write the token the grammar already has.                                                                       |
| D8   | `d8w-text-bypass`                    | statique | `expect(x.text).toContain/toMatch` short-circuits the typed accessor subject → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Assert on the accessor itself (`expect(x)`), which carries the tokens and the fixture resolution.                                       |
| D9   | `d9w-single-use-ref`                 | statique | A capture ref (`match.ref`, `{{kind#ref}}`) appearing exactly once in the whole file (code plus the referenced `_expected/` fixtures) is named for nothing → warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Drop the ref name and keep the bare token.                                                                                              |
| D12  | `d12w-response-body-probe`           | statique | A test accumulating a CLUSTER of raw probes on `.response.body` (≥ `threshold`, default 3; a variable cast from `.response.body` counts its reads) → warning: this case wants a full golden (`expect(result.response).toMatch('case.http')`). One or two probes stay silent (a legitimate scalpel).                                                                                                                                                                         | Golden the response: `expect(result.response).toMatch('<case>.http')`, with tokens for the parts that move.                             |
| D13  | `d13w-unfrozen-negative-fixture`     | statique | A `toMatch` whose FAILURE is the subject of the test must carry `{ frozen: true }` → otherwise `TEST_UPDATE=1` silently rewrites the deliberately-wrong fixture instead of throwing → warning. Two shapes: the exact wrapper (`expect(() => …).toThrow()` / `expect(…).rejects.toThrow()`) and the bounded heuristic — a golden inside a helper whose body also asserts a throw, which is where a helper owning the try/catch puts it.                                      | Pass `{ frozen: true }` so update mode never overwrites the fixture the test is about.                                                  |
| D15  | `d15w-status-only-probe`             | statique | A test whose ONLY assertions are HTTP status probes (`expect(X.status).toBe(N)` / `.toEqual(N)`, N a numeric literal 100–599) → warning: this case wants a full golden (`expect(result.response).toMatch('case.http')`). A status probe BESIDE a real assertion (a golden, `toMatchRows`, `toContain`…) stays silent (a legitimate scalpel).                                                                                                                                | Assert what the response carries, not only the code it came back with.                                                                  |
| D16  | `d16-sampled-oracle`                 | statique | No sampled value under an oracle: `new Date()` (no argument), `Date.now()`, `performance.now()`, `Math.random()` and `randomUUID()` are an error as a direct argument of `expect` or of its matcher, and anywhere inside a structural matcher's expected shape. A test that pins the clock (`clock.at`, `clock.advance`) is out of reach — the reading is then the constant it chose — and so is a `*.specification.ts(x)`, where a runner legitimately samples at startup. | Pin it with `clock.at()`, or match it with `{{iso8601}}`/`match.uuid`.                                                                  |
| D16  | `d16w-ambient-value`                 | statique | A sampled value anywhere in a test callback is a warning — the wider net around D16, silent where D16 already refuses and on a name built in a template literal. | D17  | `d17w-double-only-oracle`            | statique | A module test whose every assertion reads the call log of a double it built itself (`mockOf`, `vi.fn`, `vi.spyOn`) is a warning. The reach is the `module` role: on a component a callback prop IS the contract with its parent. It is a warning, and not an error, because one subject answers this way honestly — one whose PRODUCT is a call it was handed (a listener, an output port) — and the shape is the same one either way.                                      | Assert the returned value or the resulting state — or say in a line that the call IS the product.                                       |
| D18  | `d18w-existence-only-oracle`         | statique | A test whose ONE assertion is an existence check (`toBeDefined`, `toBeTruthy`, `not.toBeNull`, `not.toBeUndefined`, a bare `toThrow` or a bare `toHaveBeenCalled`) is a warning. | D19  | `d19w-probe-cluster`                 | statique | Three probes (`threshold`, default 3) on one goldenable subject — `stdout`, `stderr`, `content`, `head`, `meta()`, `canonical`, `alternates`, `tree`, `html` — with no `toMatch('<file>')` on it is a warning. Fixable (`--fix`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Run `jterrazz-test-check <root> --fix`; it rewrites the order.                                                                          |
| D4b  | `d4b-spec-shape`                     | checker  | A `<case>.spec.yaml` document follows its grammar: closed keys at document level (`kind`, `description`, `fixture`, `env`, `serve`, `runs`) and inside a run (`command`, `stdin`, `timeout`, `waitFor`, `exit`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `files`), `description:` and `runs:` required, `command:` and `exit:` required in every run, `exit:` an integer literal, `waitFor:` only on the last run and never with `stdin:`, a `files:` path relative and under the workdir.       | Write the key the grammar names; the message prints the accepted set.                                                                   |
| D5   | `d5-spec-volatile-literal`           | checker  | No expected output carries a literal volatile value: a loopback origin with a port (`127.0.0.1:8080`, `localhost:3000`), an absolute temporary path (`/tmp/`, `/private/tmp/`, `/var/folders/`) or a home path (`/Users/…`, `/home/…`). Both halves of the ground are judged by the one list — an expected stream of a `<case>.spec.yaml`, and every text file under `_expected/`. A `{{token}}` is not a literal.                                                          | Write the token the message names — `{{workdir}}`, `{{url}}` — in place of the literal.                                                 |
| D5   | `d5w-spec-pinned-value`              | checker  | A literal ISO-8601 timestamp or uuid in an expected stream of a `<case>.spec.yaml` → warning, unless the same value appears in a `fixture:`, a `stdin:`, a command argument or an `env:`/`serve:` value of the same document (it is then pinned, not volatile). Under `_expected/` the same class waits for D21w, whose criterion chapter 12 carries.                                                                                                                       | Token it, or seed it — a value the document pins is a value it may assert.                                                              |
| D10  | `d10w-tokens-in-requests`            | checker  | A known token in a file under `_requests/` → warning: requests are inputs, never matched.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Write the literal value the request actually sends.                                                                                     |
| D11  | `d11w-spec-silent-refusal`           | checker  | A run whose `exit:` is non-zero with neither `stdout:` nor `stderr:` → warning: the document does not say why the command refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Write the refusal the command prints — that is what the case proves.                                                                    |
| D3   | `d3-tomatch-resolves-under-expected` | runtime  | Every `toMatch` subject resolves against `_expected/` — response, stream, json, directory, tree. Only `.request()` reads `_requests/`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Put the golden under `_expected/` and name it with its extension.                                                                       |
| D7   | `d7-strict-intercepts`               | runtime  | As soon as an `api`/`jobs` chain declares an intercept, any unmatched outgoing request (an exhausted queue included) fails the spec with an explicit error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Declare the contract the request needs, or stop making the request.                                                                     |
| D14  | `d14-tomatch-fixture-name`           | runtime  | `toMatch` on an accessor subject (`stream`/`json`/`response`/tree) expects a fixture NAME (extension included): passing a `RegExp` (or any non-string) throws immediately, naming the subject and the `expect(x.text).toMatch(/re/)` escape hatch.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Write the fixture's name, or assert on `.text` when a pattern is genuinely what you mean.                                               |
| D1   | `d1-read-only-accessors`             | type     | A result accessor is read-only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Assert on what the run produced; change the Given if the answer is wrong.                                                               |
| D11  | `d11-golden-file`                    | process  | A tool's output is asserted as a full golden per scoped use case, not as a cluster of greps; `.grep()` stays the scalpel for targeted probes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Golden the stream, and keep `.grep()` for the one line a case is genuinely about.                                                       |

## E — Environment & runner configuration

| Code | Implementation                       | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Fix                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ------------------------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| E2   | `e2-preset-config`                   | statique | A `vitest.config.*` default-exports `defineSpecConfig(...)`; the call is resolved through an `export default <Identifier>` declarator, through a `satisfies`/`as` annotation, and through one `mergeConfig(defineSpecConfig(…), …)` — vitest’s own way of layering over the preset.                                                                        | Start from `defineSpecConfig()` — budgets, the artefact dir and the `_fixtures` exclusion are the preset's.                                      |
| E4   | `e4w-project-binding`                | statique | A project literal collecting `specs/<facet>/` is named `<facet>`, and one named for a facet is rooted there; `unit` collects outside `specs/`. What an include collects is read from the GLOB and the config’s own place in its package, never from the absolute path. Any other name is out of reach — a repository suite names its projects as it likes. | Name the project after the facet it collects; `{ include, exclude }` stay yours.                                                                 |
| E5   | `e5-no-simulated-dom`                | statique | A test file declares no simulated DOM: the `@vitest-environment happy-dom\|jsdom` pragma is an error. Reach: the roles that RUN a test (`module`, `component`, `specification`) — a project config is E5b’s.                                                                                                                                               | A rendered thing is a `.test.tsx` beside its component, collected by the `component()` project.                                                  |
| E6   | `e6-component-project-helper`        | statique | A browser project comes from `component()`: in a vitest config, a `browser` key under `test` that is not inside a `component(...)` call is an error. A `browser` key elsewhere (a `define`, an env registration) is not a project block and stays out of reach.                                                                                            | Replace the block with `component({ vite })` and keep only what belongs to the project.                                                          |
| E7   | `e7w-include-prefix-exists`          | statique | An `include` glob of a PROJECT — an object under `test` or in `projects`, never `optimizeDeps.include` and its kin — whose static prefix (the segments before the first wildcard, brace or bracket), resolved from the config, is not a directory is a warning.                                                                                            | Point the glob at the folder that exists, or delete the project that collects nothing.                                                           |
| E8   | `e8-literate-specification-exists`   | statique | `literate.specification`, resolved from the config directory, names a file that exists. The config directory is what the path is read against; a project that moves Vite’s `root` states its door relative to the config all the same.                                                                                                                     | Point it at the `*.specification.ts` that exports `cli`.                                                                                         |
| E9   | `e9w-env-assignment-in-test`         | statique | A test writes the process environment through `vi.stubEnv` alone: a raw assignment onto a variable of it (named or computed), a replacement of `process.env` itself, and a `delete` of one of its variables are each a warning; a `*.specification.ts(x)` is out of reach by role.                                                                         | Use `vi.stubEnv('X', 'y')`, which restores itself; a CLI default belongs to `specification.cli({ defaults })`.                                   |
| E3   | `e3-config-present`                  | checker  | Every workspace member with tests OF ITS OWN (a `test` script that does not delegate to members, or a `*.test.ts(x)` outside another package’s tree) declares a vitest config (`vitest.config.*`). The MEMBER pass judges the member itself, with or without a `specs/` root; a root that only delegates owes nothing.                                     | Write `export default defineSpecConfig()` in the member — the preset carries the budgets, the artefact directory and the `_fixtures/` exclusion. |
| E5b  | `e5b-no-simulated-dom-config-member` | checker  | `environment: 'happy-dom'\|'jsdom'` in a `vitest.config.*` is an error. The MEMBER pass is the one channel that holds it: a config is not always a file the repository's oxlint configuration collects, while the member pass starts from the root manifest and reaches every declared member — and one finding is one line in one report.                 | Remove `environment` and collect the rendered tests with `component()`.                                                                          |
| E1   | `e1-env-allowlist`                   | meta     | Every environment variable the framework reads is on the allow-list, and a dynamic read carries its sanction comment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Add the variable to `env-allowlist.ts`, or read it through the option that already exists.                                                       |

## F — Imports & protecting production

| Code | Implementation                | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---- | ----------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1   | `f1-no-subpath-import`        | statique | Everything is imported from `@jterrazz/test`; an import of `@jterrazz/test/<subpath>` is an error, except the subpaths the package's `exports` map publishes — the entries are `.`, `./vitest`, `./oxlint` and `./schema`, and the three named ones are exempt everywhere. The list is READ from the manifest, never copied into the rule, so a published entry is exempt the day it ships.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Import the name from `@jterrazz/test`; it is re-exported there by design.                                                                                                                                                   |
| F2   | `f2-no-test-imports-in-prod`  | statique | A production file never imports `vitest`, `@jterrazz/test`, a `*.test.*`, a `*.fixtures.*` or `mockOf` (one exception: `@jterrazz/test/oxlint`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Move the code that needs the import into a test, or inject what it needs as a port.                                                                                                                                         |
| F3   | `f3-specs-public-entry`       | statique | From `specs/`, only a deep import of the framework's INTERNALS is forbidden: a relative path resolving into the framework repository's `src/{specification,integrations,vitest,lint}/`, or any `@jterrazz/test/<subpath>` the package's `exports` map does not publish — the published subpaths are exempt, READ from the manifest as in F1, which holds the list. A consumer importing ITS OWN app's source is always allowed (that is the documented pattern). No folder exception: a probe that cannot reach its subject through the public entry is a module test beside its module, not a spec.                   | Reach the framework through `@jterrazz/test`, or move the probe beside the module it covers.                                                                                                                                |
| F4   | `f4-no-test-to-test-import`   | statique | A test file never imports another test file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Move what the two share into a `*.fixtures.ts` neighbour.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| F5   | `f5-fixtures-only-from-tests` | statique | A `*.fixtures.ts` is importable only from a test file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Move the value into production code if production needs it; otherwise import it from a test.                                                                                                                                |
| F6   | `f6-no-foreign-test-runtime`  | statique | A test file imports no second test runtime: `@testing-library/*`, `happy-dom`, `jsdom`, `vitest/browser`, `vitest-browser-*`, `@vitest/browser*`, `msw`, `msw/*`, `nock`, `sinon`, `vitest-mock-extended`, `jest`, `@jest/*`, `mockdate`, `playwright`, `playwright-core`, `@playwright/test`, `webdriverio` and `appium` are errors, each named with what replaces it; `react-dom/server` is one too, in the `module` role alone. Reach: the roles that RUN a test (`module`, `component`, `spec`, `specification`) — a fixture project’s config and a providers module under `specs/` legitimately name the adapter. | Go through what replaces the seam: a facet, the element vocabulary, `intercept()`, `clock` or `mockOf`.                                                                                                                     |
| F8   | `f8-no-seam-dependency`       | checker  | A member declares no dependency `@jterrazz/test` already carries (`msw`, `vitest-mock-extended`; `yaml` in devDependencies only — as a production dependency it is the product’s own library) and no retired seam (`happy-dom`, `jsdom`, `@testing-library/*`, `@playwright/test`, `mockdate`) — except `@testing-library/react-native` in a member that runs jest, where it is the only vocabulary the runtime has until the React Native answer lands. The optional peers — `playwright`, `vite`, `react`, `better-sqlite3`, `pg`, `redis`, `testcontainers`… — are declared by the consumer, by design.             | Remove the declaration: a transitive is already resolved by the package; a retired seam has a facet that replaces it (`component()`, `website()`, `clock`, `intercept()`). The diagnostic carries a sentence for each case. |

## G — Infrastructure

| Code | Implementation             | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Fix                                                                                                       |
| ---- | -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G4   | `g4-no-dom-in-module-test` | statique | A module test touches no DOM global: `document`, `window`, `navigator`, `HTMLElement` referenced in VALUE position in a `module`-role file OUTSIDE `specs/` is an error. A name in type position (`x as HTMLElement`) and a `typeof window` guard reach no document and stay out of reach. | A rendered thing is a `.test.tsx` beside its component, collected by `component()`.                       |
| G2   | `g2-per-worker-isolation`  | runtime  | Isolation is per WORKER: each worker takes its own schema, database index or file copy, so two workers never share state.                                                                                                                                                                  | Take the handle the runner gives the chain; a client opened at the default index talks to another worker. |
| G3   | `g3-docker-aware-capture`  | runtime  | The capture is docker-aware: every container a run spawned carries that run label, and the scope exit removes them whether the test asked about them or not.                                                                                                                               | Bind the result with `await using`, and declare `docker` on the runner.                                   |

## I — Source architecture

| Code | Implementation           | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Fix                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---- | ------------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| I1   | `i1-layer-boundaries`    | statique | A project DECLARES its layers under `src/` through the `layers` option (allowed packages, internal imports, one folder per dependency, seams); any import outside the declared edges is an error. With no layer map the rule is inert.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Declare the edge in the layer map, or route the import through the layer that owns it.                                                                       |
| I2   | `i2-sibling-test-naming` | statique | The test of `<file>.ts` is `<file>.test.ts` beside it; a misnamed `.test.ts`, a `__tests__/` directory or a package's `tests/` or `test/` root is an error. A RENDERED unit answers to the same law wherever it lives: a `.test.tsx` is the neighbour of the `.tsx` it renders, or of the `.ts` of the hook or DOM function whose Host it carries. A `module`-role file under a `specs/` tree is a repository suite — it covers a tree, so it has no neighbour to miss. | Put the test beside the unit it covers, under the same basename.                                                                                             |
| I4   | `i4-no-module-doubles`   | statique | A test doubles a PORT, never a module: `vi.mock`/`vi.doMock` of a specifier outside the `modules` allow-list (a config comment states why each entry is there), a `__mocks__/` or `__fixtures__/` directory, and — in a `module`-role test — importing a data asset (`.json`, `.sql`, `.yaml`, …) are all errors. A dotted specifier (`./dashboard.post`) is still code. The `vi.stubGlobal` clause moved to M3 in 16.0: one owner per convention.                      | Double the port with `mockOf<Port>()`, keep a payload in a `*.fixtures.ts` neighbour, and allow-list a native module with its reason (chapter 05 § Doubles). |

## J — Hygiene

| Code | Implementation                  | Channel  | Enforces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Fix                                                                                                  |
| ---- | ------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| J2   | `j2-no-sleep`                   | statique | No arbitrary sleep (`setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`Atomics.wait`, or a `node:timers/promises` import) in any test file — synchronisation is `see()`/`gone()` inside a scenario and `waitUntil(predicate)` everywhere else.                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Wait for the condition, not for a duration.                                                          |
| J6   | `j6w-given-in-the-test`         | statique | A `beforeEach`/`beforeAll` in a test file is a warning, and so is an `afterEach`/`afterAll` whose body does more than restore (`cleanup`, `vi.useRealTimers`, `vi.restoreAllMocks`, `vi.resetAllMocks`, `vi.unstubAllGlobals`, `vi.unstubAllEnvs`) — handed over by name (`afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks)`) or called in the body. `afterAll(cleanup)` in a `*.specification.ts` is A4's own idiom and out of reach by role. | Call a function from each test instead of a hook; `clock.at()` and `intercept()` restore themselves. |
| J10  | `j10-one-describe-level`        | upstream | At most one level of `describe` — `vitest/max-nested-describe` with `{ max: 1 }`, set by the `testing` fragment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Flatten the nesting: the test name is the sentence, and one level groups the file.                   |
| J3   | `j3w-spec-empty-assertion`      | checker  | An expected stream whose whole content is `{{any}}` → warning: the run executes and proves nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Regenerate with `TEST_UPDATE=1` and keep tokens only for the parts that move.                        |
| J4   | `j4-spec-description-unique`    | checker  | Two `<case>.spec.yaml` documents in one directory do not share a `description:`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Name what each case proves; two titles that read alike leave two files to open.                      |
| J5   | `j5-spec-description`           | checker  | A document's `description:` is a title: one line, lowercase initial (an all-caps identifier exempted), no trailing period, under 100 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Write it as a title, not as a sentence.                                                              |
| J9   | `j9-checker-suppression-reason` | checker  | Every `checker-disable-next-line` / `checker-disable-line` directive carries ` -- <reason>`, wherever a checker pass can be silenced: a test, a document, a fixture under ground. The word inside a string is prose, not a directive.                                                                                                                                                                                       | Write `checker-disable-next-line <id> -- <reason>`.                                                  |
